routes.label: Identify the arguments with rational logarithms

question: For any positive integer \(n,\) let \[ f(n)= \begin{cases} \log_8n, & \log_8n\in\mathbb{Q},\\ 0, & \log_8n\notin\mathbb{Q}. \end{cases} \] What is \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{1997}f(n)?\)
solution:
Most terms are zero, so first determine which positive integers have rational logarithms to base 8. Suppose
\[
\log_8 n=\frac{p}{q},
\]
where \(p\) is a nonnegative integer and \(q\) is a positive integer. Rewriting this as an exponential equation gives
\[
n^q=8^p=2^{3p}.
\]
If \(n\) had an odd prime factor, that prime would also divide \(n^q\), contradicting the right-hand side. Thus \(n\) must be a power of 2, including \(n=1=2^0\).

Conversely, for every nonnegative integer \(k\),
\[
\log_8(2^k)=\frac{k}{3},
\]
which is rational. This proves that we have identified all eligible arguments.

Since
\[
2^{10}=1024\le1997<2048=2^{11},
\]
these arguments are exactly \(2^0,2^1,\ldots,2^{10}\), each appearing once. All other terms contribute zero, so
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{1997}f(n)
=\frac{0+1+\cdots+10}{3}
=\frac{10\cdot11}{2\cdot3}
=\boxed{\frac{55}{3}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
